_comment: Classification rules for bump_version.py. Ordered: the first rule whose
'match' hits the line decides the action. {old} and {new} are substituted
with the version tokens; 'match' receives regex-escaped forms.
Each rewrite rule carries its own 'replace' pairs so only the construct the
rule is about is touched. Replacing every {old} on a matched line would
corrupt lines that mix a live reference with a historical statement.
'paths' restricts a rule by suffix. The heading rule needs it because '#' is
a markdown heading in .md but a comment in .sh/.yaml/.toml, where the text
is as likely to be history as a live claim.
JSON rather than YAML because these tools run in the lint job, which installs
only pre-commit; the package stays stdlib-only like
_rewrite_scope_why: The documentation surface this agent owns. Outside it, references are held
rather than rewritten, because they pin an image on purpose: examples/mlperf/
records the image a submission was validated against, and examples/models/
and tools/docker/ launchers pin what their author tested. Verified against the
v26.6 release, which left every one of those references on v26.5 while

_excluded_paths_why.release-notes.md: owned by release_notes.py, which rotates sections instead of substituting
_excluded_paths_why.docker-release/: historical build recipes; rewriting them would falsify what an old image was built from
_excluded_paths_why.tools/release_docs/: this tooling's own source, snapshots and rule files name releases as data and worked examples; scanning them put 82 self-referential items in the review list, enough to bury a real decision
_excluded_paths_why.skills/release-docs-update/: the skill's examples are illustrations, not release references
_excluded_paths_why.tests/unit_tests/release_docs/: fixtures pin old versions on purpose

rules.name: dated-changelog-entry
rules.why: a dated announcement is history: the README 'What's New' list gains a new entry per release (v26.6 prepended one in #1114) and older entries keep the tags they shipped with, so rewriting them produces 'Primus v26.6 training images: rocm/primus:v26.7'

rules.name: ci-base-image
rules.why: the CI dev image, not a published release reference: bumping it changes what CI builds against, and tools/ci/check_version_consistency.py couples the two declarations

rules.name: docker-image-tag
rules.why: published image tags always move to the new release

rules.name: dockerfile-filename
rules.why: references to the release Dockerfile track the release

rules.name: release-branch
rules.why: branch form only if the branch exists; otherwise the v26.4-style commit form

rules.name: historical-statement
rules.why: may be history to preserve rather than a claim to update

rules.name: markdown-heading
rules.why: a markdown heading naming the current release moves with it
